tasks.short: Improve how we grade, reward and develop jobs across our three sites.

today.trigger: An annual reward review, CAO change or recurring manager complaint exposes a weakness in current methods.
steps: Collect current policies, job grades, pay tables and manager feedback.
Compare practices across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo and identify differences between the two CAOs.
Discuss proposed changes with HRBPs, Payroll, Recruitment and Learning and Development.
Draft methods, test examples and prepare an approval proposal.
Explain approved changes to managers and update guidance.
drudgery: Finding the current policy and CAO versions
Rewriting the same explanation for different audiences
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow, not observed: reconciling inconsistent guidance and gathering feedback probably consume much of the preparation time.

lenses.faster: An assistant assembles a source-linked comparison of current methods and drafts changes. Approved spreadsheet rules test pay examples without manually rebuilding calculations.
lenses.autonomous: A new approved CAO or policy version triggers an impact checklist and draft revision pack. Changes to employee treatment remain subject to approval.
lenses.ambitious: Check whether job grading, pay offers and development routes support productive hires who stay beyond day 90. Review recurring exceptions across all three sites instead of waiting for the annual cycle.
lenses.joy: Remove document hunting and repetitive drafting. Keep the conversations about fair pay, workable progression and what managers need.
lenses.options: Compare three approaches to progression, including cost, CAO constraints and consequences for new hires and established staff.
lenses.altitude: Own the standards, tests and review cycle for reward methods instead of personally rebuilding every proposal.
reach: Help Recruitment define approved offer ranges
Help Learning and Development connect job grades to development routes
Help FP&A model the cost of proposed progression rules

tasks.human_edge: The specialist judges fairness and operational fit, negotiates tradeoffs and earns acceptance from managers and employee representatives.
tasks.pattern_why: Copilot: evidence gathering, drafting and scenario preparation accelerate, while policy choices and agreement stay with the specialist. Numerical checks use deterministic software.

in_practice.trigger: A policy review request or a newly approved CAO version enters the reward review register.
steps: Retrieve approved source documents with effective dates and applicable employee groups.
Draft a comparison and flag missing or conflicting provisions with source references.
Run approved pay and progression scenarios using deterministic calculations.
Have the specialist assess fairness, operational effects and required consultation.
Route the selected proposal for approval and prepare manager communications.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist validates the proposal; the HR Director approves policy, with OR involvement or consent where legally required and Payroll validation before implementation.
data_needed: Current and previous CAO and policy versions
Job families, grades and approved pay tables
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint reward review register containing sources, calculations, decisions and approvals.

evidence.claim: Language models can prepare policy comparisons and draft options from supplied documents, subject to source checking.
The estimated 40% reduction in specialist effort is a planning hypothesis for Noordhaven, not a measured result.

risks: Applying the wrong CAO, employee scope or effective date
Treating a plausible model explanation as an authoritative legal interpretation
An employment decision tool may fall within EU AI Act high-risk requirements depending on its intended use; assess this before extending beyond policy assistance
Consultation and approval delays may limit calendar-time improvement
research_questions: How much of the 53.6 annual hours is preparation rather than consultation and decision-making?
Are job grades, CAO coverage and policy versions reliable enough to support repeatable comparisons?
Can a pilot reproduce previously approved examples without material errors?
Which proposed methods require OR consent, legal review or an AI Act assessment?

tasks.short: Run fair appraisal and reward programmes that managers and the works council can support.

today.trigger: An appraisal cycle, fairness concern, employee relations issue or policy review requires a programme update.
steps: Collect programme documents, participation figures and feedback from managers and HRBPs.
Review differences in access, appraisal outcomes and reward practices across employee groups.
Develop proposed changes and discuss practical and legal implications.
Arrange OR involvement and obtain the necessary approvals.
Support implementation and evaluate results.
drudgery: Chasing programme updates from three sites
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: collecting comparable evidence is repetitive, while employee relations discussions and agreement take time that automation cannot remove.

lenses.faster: Produce a programme review pack from approved aggregate data and source-linked feedback summaries. Draft implementation materials once and adapt them for office and shift managers.
lenses.autonomous: Scheduled checks flag missed appraisal milestones or differences requiring investigation. They do not score employees or determine who deserves a promotion.
lenses.ambitious: Regularly test whether shift workers, part-time staff and employees at each site receive comparable access to progression and benefits. Connect findings to retention and manager satisfaction.
lenses.joy: Reduce status chasing and report assembly. Spend more time hearing concerns and helping managers apply programmes consistently.
lenses.options: Compare appraisal frequency, calibration methods and implementation schedules against manager workload and employee experience.
lenses.altitude: Become the owner of programme quality, fairness checks and follow-through across sites.
reach: Support HRBPs with programme evaluation
Support the HR Director with OR briefing materials
Help People Analytics define fair participation measures

tasks.human_edge: Trust, conflict resolution and judgments about fair treatment require accountable people who understand employee circumstances.
tasks.pattern_why: Copilot: AI prepares evidence, drafts materials and suggests questions; people lead employee relations, programme design and individual decisions.

in_practice.trigger: A scheduled programme review or an HRBP escalation opens a review case.
steps: Pull approved aggregate participation and outcome measures with data freshness labels.
Summarise authorised feedback, removing unnecessary personal details.
Flag differences for investigation and draft alternative programme changes.
Review findings with HRBPs and prepare the required OR and leadership materials.
Record the approved changes and evaluate their effects after implementation.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist and HRBPs validate findings; the HR Director approves changes after applicable OR and legal processes. Individual appraisal or reward decisions remain human.
data_needed: Site, job family, grade and working-hours groupings
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint programme register with analysis versions, review comments, approvals and follow-up actions.

evidence.claim: Summarisation and draft preparation can reduce administrative work around programme reviews, but cannot establish that an observed difference is discriminatory.
The estimated 35% effort saving requires validation against Noordhaven's consultation and implementation workload.

risks: Small groups may expose individual employees even in aggregate reports
Historical appraisal data may reproduce manager bias
Dutch equal-treatment rules govern any positive-action proposal; do not import US affirmative-action practices
Processing special-category data needs a valid legal basis and safeguards; do not infer ethnicity or health status
Using AI to evaluate employees or influence promotion can trigger EU AI Act high-risk requirements
research_questions: Which programme administration duties belong to this specialist rather than HRBPs?
Can existing data support useful comparisons without identifying individuals in small groups?
What evidence would distinguish programme unfairness from differences in job mix or eligibility?
How much programme effort remains tied to consultation, mediation and manager support?

tasks.short: Keep reward records and the employee handbook accurate and current.

today.trigger: An approved employee change, benefit amendment or CAO update requires a record or handbook revision.
steps: Receive the change and verify its authority and effective date.
Check the relevant AFAS record or SharePoint handbook section.
Prepare the record correction or revised wording.
Ask Payroll, HR Administration or the policy owner to verify the change.
Publish the approved version and retain the change history.
drudgery: Copying approved changes between documents and records
Finding inconsistent wording in multiple handbook sections
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: duplicate entry, version checking and approval chasing dominate routine changes; ambiguous cases take longer.

lenses.faster: Generate a handbook redline and proposed record changes directly from an approved change request. Automated checks catch missing dates, conflicting versions and incomplete fields.
lenses.autonomous: An approved change request starts validation, drafting and routing automatically. Publication and any pay-affecting record update require an authorised reviewer.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a clear change history and check all related handbook sections whenever a benefit changes. Make guidance easier for shift workers to find and understand.
lenses.joy: Remove copying, version naming and repeated reminder emails. Keep careful handling of exceptions and improving employee explanations.
lenses.options: Offer a formal policy revision, a plain-English employee explanation and a short manager FAQ from the same approved facts.
lenses.altitude: Own the rules and quality checks that keep reward records and guidance aligned.
reach: Take routine reward-record validation off HR Administration
Help Payroll maintain an approved list of reward-related changes
Help the SharePoint owner improve policy version control

tasks.human_edge: The specialist resolves ambiguous entitlements and takes responsibility for wording that employees will rely on.
tasks.pattern_why: Agent with gate: a workflow combines deterministic field checks with an LLM drafting step and routes proposed changes for approval before writing or publishing.

in_practice.trigger: A complete, approved change request arrives in the restricted HR change register.
steps: Validate employee identifiers, scope, authority and effective dates against approved rules.
Retrieve the current record and affected handbook sections using restricted access.
Prepare an AFAS change proposal and source-linked document redline.
Route the proposal to the designated record and policy approvers.
Apply approved changes through supported interfaces and retain before-and-after values.
in_practice.human_gate: HR Administration approves personnel-record writes; Payroll approves pay-affecting fields; the policy owner approves handbook publication and checks required OR processes.
systems: AFAS Profit supported interfaces, subject to permission checks
A workflow service, subject to licensing
data_needed: Relevant AFAS fields and validation rules
Current handbook and authoritative policy sources
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS change history and a restricted SharePoint change register recording source, reviewer, effective date and published version.

evidence.claim: SharePoint supports document version history and approval capabilities that can support controlled handbook maintenance.
The integrated workflow and estimated 65% effort saving are untested at Noordhaven.

risks: A wrong effective date or employee-group mapping could change pay incorrectly
Unverified AFAS write permissions or interfaces may prevent safe automation
Draft policy wording could introduce an unintended entitlement
Personnel data could reach an unauthorised model or overly broad SharePoint audience
Medical details from absence cases must not enter reward records or handbook drafting
research_questions: Which record changes can AFAS support through authorised, auditable interfaces?
Are change requests consistently approved and complete before this task begins?
Can the workflow preserve effective dates, rollback information and approval separation?
What proportion of the 42.7 annual hours concerns routine records versus substantive handbook policy?

tasks.short: Produce organisation charts, career paths and clear job-grading and pay reports.

today.trigger: A management review, restructuring proposal or career-framework update requires a report.
steps: Export reporting lines, job titles, grades and relevant pay data.
Reconcile duplicate titles, missing managers and outdated job descriptions.
Build charts, career-path summaries and compensation tables.
Check the report with HRBPs and the relevant managers.
Distribute the approved report to its intended audience.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: cleaning exports and manually maintaining charts consume most routine reporting effort.

lenses.faster: Generate recurring tables and organisation charts from a validated job hierarchy. Draft narrative commentary only after the figures pass reconciliation.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly extract triggers routine internal reports when validation passes. New career paths, sensitive disclosures and changed definitions enter a review queue.
lenses.ambitious: Keep an up-to-date view of progression routes across all sites, including required Studytube certificates. Show where approved routes are missing or hard to access.
lenses.joy: Remove chart maintenance and slide formatting. Keep interpretation and conversations about useful career opportunities.
lenses.options: Produce views by site, job family, grade and approved career route without rebuilding the report each time.
lenses.altitude: Own the job hierarchy, reporting definitions and disclosure rules behind a reliable reporting service.
reach: Maintain routine organisation reporting for People Analytics
Provide approved career-route information to Learning and Development
Provide grade-level workforce summaries to FP&A

tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides whether a career route is credible and explains sensitive grading or pay findings.
tasks.pattern_why: Deterministic software: recurring charts, tables and access rules follow approved mappings and reproducible calculations. Optional LLM commentary is checked and cannot invent career routes or figures.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract completes or a user requests an approved report template.
steps: Validate hierarchy completeness, grade mappings and extract freshness.
Generate charts and pay summaries using versioned definitions.
Apply audience permissions and suppress groups below the approved disclosure threshold.
Release validated routine reports to existing authorised audiences.
Send validation failures, new career routes and nonstandard disclosures to the specialist.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves templates, career-route definitions and audiences initially and after material changes; routine runs require intervention only for exceptions.
data_needed: Approved pay definitions and reporting periods
Approved career routes and certificate requirements
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted reporting run register linked to Power BI refresh history, validation results and released report versions.

evidence.claim: Power Query supports repeatable data transformation, and Power BI supports refreshable reports and row-level security.
evidence.source: Microsoft Excel Power Query; Microsoft Power BI

evidence.claim: The estimated 70% effort saving assumes stable job mappings and mostly recurring reports.

risks: Nightly data may omit same-day organisational changes
Incorrect reporting lines or grade mappings can make a polished report misleading
Salary summaries may reveal individuals in small groups
An apparent career path may imply progression that managers have not approved
research_questions: What share of reports repeats the same structure and definitions?
How complete and current are AFAS reporting lines and position records?
Can access and export controls prevent sensitive pay information reaching the wrong audience?
Are career routes formally approved and linked to maintained certificate requirements?

tasks.short: Research how warehouse, transport and office jobs are changing and what each job requires.

today.trigger: A new role, equipment change, hiring difficulty or grading question requires a job review.
steps: Collect existing job descriptions, vacancy evidence and relevant occupational information.
Interview jobholders and managers across the affected shifts and sites.
Observe work where needed and verify responsibilities, conditions and certificate requirements.
Compare related roles and identify changes in skills or job boundaries.
Document findings and validate them with the job owner and HRBP.
drudgery: Repeating the same comparison across sites
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: source collection and note synthesis are slow; observation and representative interviews remain necessary.

lenses.faster: Prepare source-linked research briefs and structured comparisons before interviews. Summarise authorised notes into duties, skills, working conditions and unresolved questions.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled source check creates a review alert when a chosen occupational source or internal job document changes. The specialist decides whether the change matters locally.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain current evidence on roles most affected by automation, labour shortages or certificate changes. Identify development routes that help warehouse and transport workers move into hard-to-fill jobs.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive desk research and note sorting. Keep site visits, curiosity about the work and discussions with experienced jobholders.
lenses.options: Compare different ways to divide duties between roles, with the training, grading and operational questions each would raise.
lenses.altitude: Maintain an evidence-based job framework and a research schedule focused on roles changing fastest.
reach: Provide role evidence to Recruiters writing vacancies
Help Learning and Development identify emerging skill needs
Support HRBPs with workforce redesign evidence

tasks.human_edge: Observation and trusted interviews reveal tacit skills, physical demands and differences between formal descriptions and actual work.
tasks.pattern_why: Copilot: AI accelerates research and synthesis, while the specialist establishes what is true through representative interviews, observation and source verification.

in_practice.trigger: An approved job-review request identifies a role and the decision the research must support.
steps: Retrieve current internal descriptions and approved external sources, recording dates and scope.
Draft a comparison and an interview guide that separates evidence from assumptions.
Collect representative jobholder and manager input across relevant sites and shifts.
Structure authorised notes and flag conflicting or unsupported claims.
Validate the final job findings with the job owner before updating the job framework.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist verifies material claims and observation findings; the job owner validates duties, while formal grading or safety changes follow their own approval processes.
data_needed: Current job descriptions and approved grades
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint job evidence library with source references, validation dates and named job owners.

evidence.claim: Language models can structure supplied interview notes and compare documents, but local job requirements still require verification.
The estimated 45% effort saving depends on the balance between desk research and site observation.

risks: Generic occupational descriptions may miss local duties, physical demands or CAO distinctions
Day-shift or manager-only interviews may misrepresent the job
External trends may be outdated or irrelevant to Dutch logistics
Interview recording or transcription may exceed the agreed privacy purpose
AI suggestions must not determine safety-critical qualification requirements
research_questions: How much research time is desk work versus interviews and observation?
Which sources provide reliable, current evidence for Dutch logistics roles?
Do current descriptions accurately represent night shifts and all three sites?
Can a pilot brief distinguish verified duties from assumptions without material omissions?

tasks.short: Build practical questionnaires and interview guides for consistent job analysis.

today.trigger: A job evaluation or organisational change requires a new or improved way to capture job evidence.
steps: Define the decision the instrument must support and the job groups it must cover.
Review existing questionnaires and the approved job-evaluation method.
Draft questions, examples and instructions.
Pilot the instrument with jobholders and managers from relevant sites and shifts.
Revise the instrument and agree how evidence will be assessed.
drudgery: Reusing questions by copying between files
Writing examples for each job family
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: drafting and organising pilot feedback are repetitive, while testing whether questions measure the right things needs specialist judgment.

lenses.faster: Draft questionnaires from an approved factor framework and generate role-specific examples. Automatically check missing factors, duplicate questions and inconsistent instructions.
lenses.autonomous: A new job-analysis request produces a draft instrument from the approved question bank. Unclear or incomplete responses generate clarification prompts for human review.
lenses.ambitious: Test whether the instrument captures physical work, responsibility and tacit skills consistently across office and shift roles. Maintain evidence on which questions produce useful answers.
lenses.joy: Remove form formatting and repeated wording changes. Keep instrument design, pilots and learning how people describe their work.
lenses.options: Compare a short questionnaire, a guided interview and an observation checklist against completion burden and evidence quality.
lenses.altitude: Own a tested question bank and the standards for reliable job evidence.
reach: Help HRBPs conduct consistent job interviews
Give Recruiters a clearer role-intake questionnaire
Help People Analytics improve survey and form quality

tasks.human_edge: The specialist judges whether questions capture job value fairly and whether people with different literacy or language needs can answer them.
tasks.pattern_why: Copilot: drafting and consistency checks are repeatable, but validity, accessibility and acceptance require pilots and specialist judgment.

in_practice.trigger: A job-review request specifies the approved evaluation framework and respondent groups.
steps: Select relevant approved questions and map them to evaluation factors.
Draft plain-language instructions and examples without changing factor definitions.
Check coverage, duplication, reading difficulty and unnecessary personal questions.
Pilot with representative respondents and compare how different reviewers interpret the answers.
Approve a versioned instrument and retain pilot findings for the next revision.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves the instrument after pilot review; any change to formal evaluation factors or scoring follows the applicable CAO and governance process.
data_needed: Existing question bank and factor definitions
Role examples validated by job owners
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint instrument library containing factor mappings, version history, pilot evidence and approval records.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft questionnaire variants and check coverage against a supplied framework; this does not establish measurement validity.
The estimated 45% effort saving assumes reusable approved questions and a manageable pilot cycle.

risks: Leading questions may favour office work over operational work
Simplification or translation may change the meaning of evaluation factors
Automatic scoring could influence pay or progression without valid evidence and appropriate AI Act assessment
Forms may collect unnecessary personal or health information
Licensed evaluation methods may restrict reuse or uploading
research_questions: Is there an approved evaluation framework and permission to use its materials in the proposed tools?
Do pilots produce consistent interpretations across sites, shifts and job families?
Which questions create missing, vague or contradictory answers today?
Does the revised instrument reduce completion effort while preserving evidence quality?

tasks.short: Turn workforce, pay and labour-market data into reliable advice for management and required reports.

today.trigger: A management question, budgeting request or authorised external reporting requirement needs analysis.
steps: Clarify the question, audience, reporting period and required definitions.
Gather AFAS data, agency figures and relevant external statistics.
Reconcile populations, hours, pay components and reporting periods.
Analyse differences and prepare findings with limitations.
Validate the analysis and obtain approval before sharing.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: reconciliation and definition disputes consume more effort than producing charts; external release may add approval delays.

lenses.faster: Reuse approved data transformations and calculations, then draft commentary from the verified results. Stop manually rebuilding agency and AFAS comparisons for each question.
lenses.autonomous: A recurring reporting request starts extraction, reconciliation and draft preparation. Unreconciled totals or changed definitions stop the workflow for review.
lenses.ambitious: Compare reward costs with offer acceptance, day-90 retention and productive hiring by role and site. Treat these as associations requiring investigation, rather than proof that pay caused the outcome.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet repair and repeated reconciliation. Keep asking useful questions and explaining what the numbers can support.
lenses.options: Show alternative assumptions for seasonal flex demand, pay progression and benefit uptake, with costs and uncertainties.
lenses.altitude: Own trusted reward measures and the interpretation standards used in workforce decisions.
reach: Support FP&A with workforce cost scenarios
Support the Controller with reward-cost reconciliation
Support People Analytics with compensation definitions and quality rules

tasks.human_edge: The specialist selects meaningful comparisons, challenges causal claims and takes responsibility for sensitive interpretation and disclosure.
tasks.pattern_why: Agent with gate: deterministic transformations produce reconciled figures, an LLM drafts the explanation, and the specialist approves conclusions and release.

in_practice.trigger: An approved analysis request or reporting calendar entry defines the audience and purpose.
steps: Load authorised extracts and external sources with reporting dates and definitions.
Run versioned joins, calculations and reconciliations, keeping agency workers distinct from employees.
Stop on material data failures and route them to the relevant data owner.
Draft findings from validated tables, linking each numerical claim to its calculation.
Obtain specialist approval and recipient-specific disclosure approval before release.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves interpretation; Finance validates financial reconciliations where relevant, and the authorised owner approves any external submission.
data_needed: Employee, grade, hours and pay-component data
Dated external benchmarks and population definitions
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint analysis register containing source snapshots, transformation versions, reconciliations and release approvals.

evidence.claim: Power Query and Power BI support reusable transformations and reporting calculations.
evidence.source: Microsoft Excel Power Query; Microsoft Power BI

evidence.claim: The estimated 50% effort saving depends on reusable definitions and access to consistent agency exports.

risks: Agency invoice costs and employee gross pay are not directly comparable
Nightly extracts and portal exports may describe different periods
Small cohorts or linked datasets may reveal individual compensation
Correlation between reward and retention may be presented as causation
An external submission may use prescribed definitions that differ from internal dashboards
research_questions: Which analyses recur often enough to justify maintained transformations?
Can all three agencies supply consistent hours, worker counts and cost components?
Do reward totals reconcile to Payroll and Finance within agreed tolerances?
Are productive-hire and day-90 measures sufficiently defined to support useful comparisons?

tasks.short: Teach managers and employees how pay, benefits and job grading work.

today.trigger: A CAO or benefit change, onboarding need or recurring misunderstanding requires training.
steps: Agree the learning need and audience with Learning and Development.
Gather approved policy wording and realistic questions from managers and employees.
Prepare slides, examples, exercises and reference materials.
Deliver sessions at times that cover relevant sites and shifts.
Review questions and learning feedback and update the materials.
drudgery: Updating repeated examples after policy changes
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: material preparation and coordination are reducible; live explanation, practice and sensitive questions remain substantial.

lenses.faster: Draft lessons, worked examples and quizzes from approved policies, using deterministic calculations for pay examples. Reuse a reviewed core module across sites.
lenses.autonomous: An approved policy revision creates a list of affected learning materials and draft updates. Existing Studytube enrolment and reminder functions handle administration where configured.
lenses.ambitious: Provide short, accessible explanations for common reward questions throughout onboarding and progression. Test understanding instead of counting course completion alone.
lenses.joy: Remove slide maintenance and repeated basic drafting. Keep useful conversations, practical exercises and helping people understand their payslip or progression route.
lenses.options: Compare a manager workshop, a short self-service module and shift briefings, with language and accessibility variants.
lenses.altitude: Own reward-learning outcomes and the accuracy of reusable content, working with Learning and Development on delivery.
reach: Take ownership of reward content within onboarding
Provide Payroll with approved educational answers to recurring questions
Help Learning and Development assess understanding of reward policies

tasks.human_edge: The specialist notices confusion, handles sensitive pay questions with care and adapts explanations to the audience.
tasks.pattern_why: Copilot: AI drafts and adapts materials, while the specialist validates content and leads teaching that requires judgment, trust and discussion.

in_practice.trigger: Learning and Development approves a training request or a policy owner approves a relevant change.
steps: Retrieve approved policy sources and define the learning outcomes and audience.
Draft a lesson, realistic examples and quizzes, calculating numerical answers with approved rules.
Review accuracy, language, accessibility and separation of general guidance from personal advice.
Publish approved materials in Studytube and schedule appropriate live sessions.
Review understanding and recurring questions, then revise content through the same approval process.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves reward content and examples; Learning and Development approves delivery design, and Payroll verifies payroll-specific explanations.
data_needed: Fictional or safely anonymised worked examples
Aggregated quiz results and recurring questions
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint learning-content register linked to Studytube course versions and aggregated evaluation results.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft lessons, examples and quizzes from supplied policy material, with expert review needed for accuracy.
The estimated 35% effort saving assumes preparation is a substantial share of the task and live delivery remains human.

risks: An incorrect worked example may be understood as a pay promise
Translation may distort a CAO entitlement or eligibility rule
Completion records may be mistaken for evidence of understanding
Personal pay or absence questions could expose sensitive information in group sessions
Self-service materials may be inaccessible to workers without convenient device access
research_questions: How much of the 32.9 annual hours is preparation, administration and live delivery?
Which recurring reward questions cause the most confusion or Payroll contacts?
Can shift workers access the materials in suitable languages and formats?
Do reviewed AI-assisted materials improve quiz performance and reduce repeat questions?

role.altitude: Become the owner of Noordhaven's reward standards, job framework and control processes, using reliable evidence to improve fairness, progression and productive hiring.
reach: Recruitment: maintain approved offer ranges and explain reward packages
HR Administration: validate routine reward records and handbook changes
Payroll: maintain approved reward rules and educational guidance
People Analytics: own compensation definitions and routine reward reports
Learning and Development: connect approved career routes, certificates and reward education
FP&A and Controller: provide reconciled reward-cost scenarios and workforce assumptions
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks total 335.1 hours a year, about 21% of the implied 1,600-hour role. The proposed effort savings total about 160 hours, worth roughly EUR 12,000 at EUR 75/hour before build, licensing, review and maintenance costs; this is capacity, not a cash saving. Savings and speedups are untested planning estimates: speedups include execution and human review, so they differ from reductions in human effort. Consultation, interviews, teaching and approvals limit elapsed-time gains. The remaining role workload has not been assessed.
skills_to_grow: Translate CAO provisions into versioned rules with Payroll and legal validation
Design job frameworks and test job-analysis instruments
Use Power Query and Power BI for reproducible, reconciled reward analysis
Specify access controls, data minimisation and audit records under AVG/GDPR
Verify AI outputs against sources and assess employment-tool uses under the EU AI Act
Run small pilots that measure total effort, errors and employee understanding
Explain reward tradeoffs clearly to managers, employees and the OR
role.ambitious_version: Build a maintained reward and progression service across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo: consistent offer ranges, trustworthy job and pay information, visible development routes and understandable employee guidance. Work with Recruitment, Payroll, Learning and Development and FP&A to test whether changes improve offer acceptance, week-one readiness and day-90 retention, while keeping individual employment decisions accountable to people.
